\paragraph{Graph neural network.}
A two-layer mean-aggregation network (hidden width 16) on the observed graph, with the node's own treatment, the mean neighbour treatment and the standardised log degree as inputs; weight decay and epochs were chosen by a graph-cluster hold-out with a corner loss, as for the other Tier A learners, and the estimate is the difference of its predictions at $(z,f)=(1,1)$ and $(0,0)$. It ran on Tier A cells with Bernoulli assignment, noise 0.5 and spillover share 0.5, mechanisms (a)--(f) and the null column, on the same assignments and graphs as the other learners but the first 10 of the 40 assignments of each of five graph draws (50 draws; on the real graphs the first 50 of 200 assignments), which every estimator in the comparison uses. The SBM cell with $d=80$ and $p=0.25$ did not finish (about four hours per cell) and is absent; 13 cells give 91 cell--mechanism rows. Median RMSE (normalised error) over the rows is 0.22 for the regression, 0.33 for the network, 0.40 for boosting, 0.41 for the adaptive H\'ajek, 0.42 for forests, 0.46 for lasso, 0.50 for DM and 0.62 for ridge; mean ranks (1 is best) are 1.8 for the regression, 3.4 for the network, then 4.4 to 6.1 for the others, and the regression is best in 59 rows, DM in 18 and the network in 2. The paired log RMSE ratio of the network to DM has an interval below zero in 57 rows and above in 27 (median $-0.25$), and to the regression below in 5 and above in 66 (median $+0.37$); the five rows below are cells of mechanism (d), where the mean log ratio to the regression is $-0.10$. On the null column the network is worse than DM (mean log ratio $+1.69$). These results concern one architecture without tuning of its width or depth; a larger or differently built network is not excluded, and it was not run on Tier G or on cluster designs.

\paragraph{Cluster designs.}
Figure~\ref{fig:cluster} compares graph-cluster designs with Bernoulli assignment (Section~\ref{sec:cluster}). The cluster-bootstrap interval ($B=100$, whole clusters resampled) covers in 83\% of the 396 cluster cells. The 78 comparisons at $d=20$ exclude the weak-mixing SBM, which has no Bernoulli arm; against cluster DM alone the regression is better in 77 of 96. Cluster regression beats cluster DM in all 16 comparisons for (c) and (e) and in 13--15 for (a), (b), (f), and it beats the Bernoulli regression in all 13 comparisons for (d). H\'ajek is undefined in draws with an empty arm, which are excluded from its summary. Unnormalised Horvitz--Thompson estimators with exposure at least 0.75 or 1 of neighbours treated, run on the 22 cluster runs (132 cells: the six mechanisms at $s=0.5$ on BA, ER, SBM, Stanford3 and ego-Facebook), are never better than the regression or cluster DM; their median log RMSE ratios to the regression are 1.66 and 2.66, and to cluster DM 1.05 and 2.64.
